subject: MAP: benchmark scope, stress profiles, and pass/fail matrix (latency/TTFT/concurrency)
messages:
From: Samuel Nguyen <samuel.nguyen@acme.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf targets and workload details

Thanks for the kick-off yesterday. Per our internal alignment, here's the minimal benchmarking scope we'd like Redwood to validate in the MAP: 

- Workload slices:
  - Chat Interactive (primary): multi-turn assistant, avg turn length 60 tokens, 95% of sessions <= 6 turns.
  - Batch summarization (secondary): 1K docs / run, average doc size 8KB, single-shot summarization.

- Traffic profile & concurrency:
  - Expected sustained QPS: 12 requests/sec for chat slice (steady state).
  - Peak concurrency target to validate: 200 concurrent sessions (user sessions, each with KV cache).

- Latency & TTFT SLOs (prelim):
  - Chat: p50 <= 40ms per call (infrastructure hop), p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms. TTFT (time-to-first-token) p90 <= 150ms.
  - Batch: throughput goal 1200 docs/hour with median response latency per document <= 1.2s.

- Acceptance criteria:
  - No more than 2% of requests exceed p99 targets during 30-minute steady-state runs.
  - No correctness regressions (we'll provide a 200-case eval set).

I've attached our rough workload spreadsheet (acme_map_workload_v1.xlsx). A few clarifications we need from Redwood: how you define TTFT precisely in the MAP, warm-up procedures (cache prefill), and whether you can run the KV cache behavior with a realistic session re-use model.

Would appreciate a short runbook and proposed timeline so we can line up our QA and procurement.

— Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme Systems
(650) 555-0198

--- Forwarded message ---

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:19:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MAP bench plan (draft) — mapping Acme targets to test plan

Team — draft plan to scope the MAP benchmarking work for Acme. High level then action items. Please comment inline.

1) Key definitions and assumptions
- TTFT: measured from request arrival at the Redwood edge to the first byte of model-generated token at the client-facing stream (includes network hop and model scheduling). We'll capture both edge-to-first-byte and server-local-to-first-byte to separate network noise.
- Concurrency model: we will model "user sessions" (long-lived KV caches). For the chat slice we will maintain session affinity; we will also run a separate test that simulates cold-start sessions.
- Warm-up: 10-minute warm-up with representative prompts drawn from Acme's eval set (see attachment).

2) Workload profiles (mapped to Acme spreadsheet)
- Chat-interactive profile: 12 qps sustained, burst to 50 qps for 5 minutes, 200 concurrent sessions with per-session KV cache size typical to 6 turns. Token distribution: mean 60, 95th 180.
- Batch summarization profile: 1K doc runs, parallelism 30 workers, aim for sustained throughput target.

3) Success criteria (pass/fail matrix) — REDWOOD proposal
- Functional gate: accuracy check using the 200-case eval (must match baseline quality threshold within tolerance).
- Latency gates (during 30-min steady-state):
  - p50 <= 45ms (edge-to-token), p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms for chat.
  - TTFT p90 <= 170ms.
  - Batch per-doc median <= 1.4s.
- Stability gate: error rate < 0.5% (5xx, OOM, queue drops).
- Concurrency gate: system should sustain 200 sessions with <5% degradation vs baseline p95.

4) Instrumentation & artifacts we will deliver
- Raw logs (token-level timestamps), aggregated percentiles, concurrency heatmaps, KV cache hit-rate over time.
- A short runbook: steps to reproduce the run, configs (model variant, quantization, batch size).
- Bench artifacts will be attached as a PDF and a CSV of per-run metrics (rwd_bench_template.csv).

5) Test variants to run (order)
A. Canary (10m): single-model, low-concurrency sanity check.
B. Warmed steady-state (30m): warm-up + 30m steady-state at target qps and concurrency.
C. Burst + recovery (20m): 5m peak burst, observe tail-latency and recovery profile.
D. Cold-start mix (15m): simulate 40% cold sessions to validate cache dynamics.

6) Timeline & responsibilities (proposed)
- Mon 2026-11-23: internal alignment + bench infra reservation (Jonas)
- Tue 2026-11-24: canary run + deliver preliminary numbers (Tessa)
- Wed 2026-11-25: full steady-state + artifacts + pass/fail report (Jonas + Karthik)
- Fri 2026-11-26: joint review + final acceptance note from Acme + DocuSign for MAP closure (Marissa to coordinate procurement)

7) Risks & mitigations
- Cold-cache tail risks: we will include prefill scenarios and quantify the delta.
- Quantization/accuracy tradeoffs: will run both FP16 and int8 candidate paths and include quality comparison.

Action items:
- Jonas: confirm infra slot and model variant (+ any kernel pinning we should try).
- Karthik: propose batch/queue knobs (batch time windows, prefetch threads).
- Marissa: prepare MAP document and DocuSign link once numbers look good.

Attachments: acme_map_workload_v1.xlsx, rwd_bench_template.csv

— Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP bench plan (draft) — mapping Acme targets to test plan

Looks good — a couple of practical tweaks from the runtime side: 

- KV cache warmup: use a 3-phase prefill (10%, 50%, 100% keys) to capture non-linear behavior; capture hit-rate per session bucket.
- Per-session memory: include an OOM-injection run at 220 concurrent sessions to validate graceful degradation.
- Kernel selection: pin a small set of optimized kernels for the canary (keeps variability low) and then run a best-effort kernel-autoselect for the full run to show production behavior.
- Measurement note: record both edge RTT (client -> edge -> first token) and intra-cluster scheduling latency; we'll publish both so Acme can see where optimizations land.

I'll claim the infra reservation and lead the canary + steady-state. Karthik, can you confirm the batch timing windows and whether you want to run quantized int8 in parallel? If yes, we should give Acme a small note about expected accuracy delta.

— Jonas
Perf & Infra Lead
